exposure: Antenatal detection of fetal growth restriction (FGR)
fetal weight less than the 2.3rd centile
antenatal detection of fetal growth restriction (FGR)
cohort: 2425 children born with FGR between September 1st 2012 and August 31st 2015
finding: The study found an association between antenatal detection of fetal growth restriction and an increased risk of gastrointestinal/urogenital and respiratory disorders, potentially due to the higher likelihood of prematurity in detected cases, while also observing a lower risk of stillbirth.
mod_finding: Detected infants were more often born after induction or caesarean section (OR 5.19, 95% CI 4.13-6.51, P < 0.0001).
